subproblems.title: Tangent space, continuity of the inverse and secant estimate in a submanifold chart (Simon Ch. 2, §4) [accepted dsmc_chart_tangentSpace_eq_range, reused]
subproblems.statement:
Let P, r, d ∈ ℕ with r ≥ 1, N ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P a chart of N as in IsEmbeddedSubmanifold. That is, ψ is C^r on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) is injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V, with q := ψ(v) and A := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v, the following hold.
(i) The classical tangent space T_qN = tangentSpace N q (velocities γ'(0) of curves γ that are C¹ on (−1, 1) with γ((−1, 1)) ⊆ N and γ(0) = q) equals A(ℝ^d).
(ii) For every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that v' ∈ V and |ψ(v') − q| < δ imply |v' − v| < ε.
(iii) For every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every y ∈ N with |y − q| < δ admits some a ∈ ℝ^d with |y − q − Aa| ≤ ε|y − q|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P r d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → ∀ v ∈ V, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v) ∧ (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ v' ∈ V, dist (ψ v') (ψ v) < δ → dist v' v < ε) ∧ (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ N, dist y (ψ v) < δ → ∃ a : Euclid d, ‖y - ψ v - fderiv ℝ ψ v a‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - ψ v‖)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Accepted node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.mean_curvature_monotonicity-a1.chart_tangent_space-a1 (candidate 44afba4d4bb9), reused with byte-identical name and frozen type; its accepted proof, condensed:
Notation: q := ψ(v), A := Dψ(v); ψ is continuous on V and differentiable on V (C^r, r ≥ 1).
1. A is injective, so there is m > 0 with |Aa| ≥ m|a| for all a (minimum of |Aa| on the compact unit sphere; m := 1 if d = 0).
2. (ii). Otherwise there are ε > 0 and v_j ∈ V with ψ(v_j) → q and |v_j − v| ≥ ε. K := {ψ(v_j)} ∪ {q} is compact and ⊆ W, so V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact (properness) and contains every v_j; a subsequence converges to some v* ∈ V. By continuity ψ(v*) = q = ψ(v), so v* = v by injectivity, contradicting |v_j − v| ≥ ε.
3. Differentiability at v: for η > 0 there is ρ(η) > 0 with |ψ(v') − q − A(v' − v)| ≤ η|v' − v| when |v' − v| < ρ(η). With η = m/2 and step 1: |v' − v| ≤ (2/m)|ψ(v') − q|.
4. (iii). Given ε > 0 let η := min(m/2, εm/2) and ρ := min(ρ(η), ρ(m/2)). By (ii) take δ₁ with |v' − v| < ρ whenever v' ∈ V and |ψ(v') − q| < δ₁, and δ₂ with ball(q, δ₂) ⊆ W. If y ∈ N and |y − q| < min(δ₁, δ₂), then y ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V), y = ψ(v'), and a := v' − v satisfies |y − q − Aa| ≤ η|v' − v| ≤ (2η/m)|y − q| ≤ ε|y − q|.
5. tangentSpace N q ⊆ A(ℝ^d). Let w = γ'(0) for a C¹ curve γ in N with γ(0) = q. By (iii), for small t ≠ 0, dist((γ(t) − q)/t, A(ℝ^d)) ≤ ε|γ(t) − q|/|t|; letting t → 0 gives dist(w, A(ℝ^d)) ≤ ε|w| for every ε > 0. A(ℝ^d) is a closed subspace, so w ∈ A(ℝ^d).
6. A(ℝ^d) ⊆ tangentSpace N q. For a = 0 use the constant curve. For a ≠ 0 choose closedBall(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V, c := ρ₀/|a| and h(t) := t/(1 + t²/c²) (C^∞, h(0) = 0, h'(0) = 1, |h| ≤ c/2). Then γ(t) := ψ(v + h(t)a) is a C¹ curve in ψ(V) ⊆ N with γ(0) = q and γ'(0) = Aa (chain rule).
7. Steps 5–6 give (i); steps 2 and 4 give (ii) and (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: Injectivity of A = Dψ(v) gives m > 0 with |Aa| ≥ m|a|.
Properness and injectivity of ψ on V give continuity of ψ⁻¹ at q (sequential compactness).
Differentiability at v plus continuity of ψ⁻¹ give the secant estimate |y − q − Aa| ≤ ε|y − q| for y ∈ N near q.
Along a C¹ curve in N, the secant estimate puts γ'(0) in the closed subspace A(ℝ^d); conversely the curves t ↦ ψ(v + h(t)a) realize every Aa.

subproblems.title: An embedded submanifold is Borel and meets small closed balls in compact sets [accepted dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed, reused]
subproblems.statement: Let P, r, d ∈ ℕ and M ⊆ ℝ^P with IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M, i.e. every y ∈ M has open sets V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W and a map ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P that is C^r on V and injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(v) injective for v ∈ V. Then (a) M is a (Borel) measurable subset of ℝ^P, and (b) every y ∈ M has some ε > 0 such that M ∩ closedBall(y, ε) is compact.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Accepted node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.regular_point_density-a1.locally_closed-a1 (candidate 6da66b1edf6f), reused with byte-identical name and frozen type; its accepted proof, condensed:
1. (Chart slices.) Let (V, W, ψ) be a chart at y ∈ M and K ⊆ W compact. Then M ∩ K = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K)): a point of M ∩ K lies in W ∩ M = ψ(V), and conversely ψ(V) ⊆ M. V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact by properness and ψ is continuous on V, so M ∩ K is compact.
2. (b). Choose r' > 0 with ball(y, r') ⊆ W and put ε := r'/2. closedBall(y, ε) is compact and ⊆ W, so M ∩ closedBall(y, ε) is compact by step 1.
3. Let O := ⋃_{y∈M} W_y over chosen charts; O is open and M ⊆ O.
4. M = O ∩ closure(M). Let p ∈ O ∩ closure(M), p ∈ W_y, ball(p, r') ⊆ W_y. C := M ∩ closedBall(p, r'/2) is compact by step 1, hence closed. Since ball(p, r'/2) is open, p ∈ closure(ball(p, r'/2) ∩ M) ⊆ closure(C) = C ⊆ M.
5. (a). M is the intersection of an open and a closed set, hence Borel. ∎
proof_key_steps: Chart slices: for compact K ⊆ W, M ∩ K = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K)) is compact by properness and continuity of ψ on V.
A closed ball around y inside the chart domain W meets M in a compact set.
With O the union of the chart domains, M = O ∩ closure(M), so M is Borel.

1. (Span of a range.) For a continuous linear D : ℝ^m → ℝ^P the set range D is the carrier of the linear subspace LinearMap.range D, so span(range D) = range D (LinearMap.coe_range, Submodule.span_eq).

2. (Projection formula.) Let D : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be linear and injective, D* its adjoint and G := D*D : ℝ^m → ℝ^m.
 (a) G is injective: if Gw = 0 then |Dw|² = ⟨D*Dw, w⟩ = ⟨Gw, w⟩ = 0, so Dw = 0 and w = 0 by injectivity of D. An injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^m is bijective (LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective), hence a unit of the ring L(ℝ^m) (ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_iff_bijective).
 (b) Put R := D ∘ G⁻¹ ∘ D*, where G⁻¹ = Ring.inverse G. Let h ∈ ℝ^P and y := G⁻¹D*h; then Gy = D*h (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel) and Rh = Dy ∈ range D. For every x ∈ ℝ^m, ⟨h − Dy, Dx⟩ = ⟨D*(h − Dy), x⟩ = ⟨D*h − Gy, x⟩ = 0, so h − Rh is orthogonal to range D. By the characterization of the orthogonal projection (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero: u ∈ K and h − u ⊥ K imply P_K h = u), (range D).starProjection h = Rh. Hence (range D).starProjection = D ∘ (D*D)⁻¹ ∘ D*.

3. (Chart data.) Let y ∈ M and let (V, W, ψ) be a chart at y given by IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M: V ⊆ ℝ^m and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, y ∈ W, ψ C¹ on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for compact K ⊆ W, Dψ(z) injective for z ∈ V. Since y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), y = ψ(v₀) with v₀ ∈ V. By chart_tangent (r = 1) and step 1, S_{ψ(v)} = span(range Dψ(v)) = range Dψ(v) for every v ∈ V, and ψ⁻¹ is continuous in the sense (ii) at every ψ(v), v ∈ V.

4. (Part (a).) Let x ∈ M; take a chart at x as in step 3 and write x = ψ(v), v ∈ V. Then S_x = range Dψ(v), and since Dψ(v) is injective, dim range Dψ(v) = dim ℝ^m = m (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).

5. (Part (b).) Fix y ∈ M and a chart as in step 3, y = ψ(v₀). Write D(v) := Dψ(v).
 (a) Since ψ is C¹ on the open set V, v ↦ D(v) is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). The adjoint A ↦ A* is a linear isometry, hence continuous, so v ↦ D(v)* is continuous on V, and so is v ↦ G(v) := D(v)*D(v) (composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous, ContinuousOn.clm_comp).
 (b) Each G(v), v ∈ V, is a unit by step 2(a), and inversion is continuous at every unit of the complete normed ring L(ℝ^m) (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt). Hence v ↦ G(v)⁻¹ and R(v) := D(v)G(v)⁻¹D(v)* are continuous on V; as V is open, R is continuous at v₀.
 (c) By step 2(b) and step 3, P_{ψ(v)} = (range D(v)).starProjection = R(v) for every v ∈ V.
 (d) Let ε > 0. Choose ρ > 0 with ‖R(v) − R(v₀)‖ < ε whenever |v − v₀| < ρ (continuity at v₀). By (ii) choose δ₁ > 0 such that v ∈ V and |ψ(v) − y| < δ₁ imply |v − v₀| < ρ. Since W is open choose δ₂ > 0 with ball(y, δ₂) ⊆ W. Let x ∈ M with |x − y| < min(δ₁, δ₂). Then x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), so x = ψ(v) with v ∈ V and |v − v₀| < ρ, whence ‖P_x − P_y‖ = ‖R(v) − R(v₀)‖ < ε by (c). So x ↦ P_x is continuous within M at y; y ∈ M was arbitrary.

6. (Part (c).) Let X be C¹. Then x ↦ DX(x) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), so x ↦ P_x ∘ DX(x) is continuous on M by (b) (ContinuousOn.clm_comp).
